AUTHOR: Mathias
TITLE: Deep Neural Network Driven Automated Underwater Object Detection
REGION: Multiple public sources (Fish4Knowledge Taiwan, Western Australia OzFish/UWA, Bali, tropical Australia DeepFish)
DATA: LifeCLEF 2015 (F4K), UWA dataset (OzFish, ref 19), Bubble Vision Bali diving video, DeepFish
V_EV: no statement found (only restoration metrics: Table 2 'PSNR MSE SSIM EPI' for DLIR pre-processing; no visibility measurement of data)
D2: UWA: 2180 train / 1020 test frames; DeepFish: 30% validated and tested
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'comprises 4418 video sequences ... Among these, around 2180 frames are used as training frames and 1020 frames are subjected to testing.'
R_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'The performance analysis is shown for the LCF-15 dataset, UWA dataset, Bubble Vision dataset and the DeepFish dataset in Fig. 7' (training data per dataset not described; no cross-dataset design stated)
C_EV: Sec. 3: 'The threshold is set to 0.4 in our experiments for appropriate box generation.'
E_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'The accuracy for fish identification is 98.5 percent, 96.77 percent, 97.99 percent and 95.3 percent respectively' (plus tracking error, IoU only)
ARCH: DLIR restoration (DCP + diffraction correction) + BEMD-GMM foreground + VGGNet-16 transfer learning, OR-combined with YOLOv3 (Darknet-53)
METR: Accuracy, recall, precision, average tracking error, IoU, FPS; PSNR/MSE/SSIM/EPI for restoration
NOTE: Inclusion via OzFish (UWA) and DeepFish field datasets; LifeCLEF is benchmark-only and Bubble Vision is web diving video. Training/test design is poorly described: only UWA frame counts and 'DeepFish 30% validated and tested'; coded image/frame random per rule for counts of images from videos. Unclear whether models were trained per dataset, so no cross-domain evaluation can be confirmed (R1=N). Threshold 0.4 justified only verbally. V5 '기타' = PSNR/SSIM of restoration, not visibility characterization.
